Using mobile data where available can help you stay connected while your service is offline. Minimise disruption to your routine by download
outages.provider_outage_information:
FTTB‑to‑FTTP sites are now included in the Complex MDU technology upgrade program. Applicable FTTB‑to‑FTTP sites will utilise spare fibre capacity available within the lead‑in cable. A planned customer‑impacting CRQ is required to implement the solution.

As part of the upgrade, hardware will be installed upstream of the DSLAM node to intercept the lead‑in Hub‑sheath Segment Distribution (HSD) cables, enabling FTTP connectivity via the spare fibres.

outage_updates.long_update:
nbn® is completing upgrades on the nbn network in your area. This will cause your nbn service to lose connection.
Using mobile data where available can help you stay connected while your service is offline. Minimise disruption to your routine by downloading required files and switching to offline work modes.

outages.notification_description:
nbn® is completing scheduled works on the nbn network in your area. This will cause your nbn service to lose connection.  

Using mobile data where available can help you stay connected while your service is offline. Minimise disruption to your routine
outages.provider_outage_information:
These planned works are part of a broader program aimed at addressing performance degradation issues on the HFC network. Activities may include optimising the alignment between the inside plant and the node, refining the alignment from the node to downstream amplifiers, and adjusting network amplifier configurations. The scope of work may also involve replacing TAPs and HFC cabling where necessary.

Customers may experience service interruptions at any point during the change window, depending on their location within the network cascade. Please refer to the interruption table in this notice for more details.

outages.provider_outage_information:
As part of a new trial, nbn is installing battery backup equipment at selected HFC nodes. When a node loses power, customers lose service even if their premises still have electricity. Battery backup will provide power resilience to nodes during planned or unplanned power related network outages.

During this planned outage to install the battery backup, end users may experience multiple service interruptions within the outage window while work is underway.

Due to safety, noise, lighting and power authority requirements, work must be performed during the day. Please refer to the scheduled dates and times for further information.
